s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity numbness and weakness with foot drop
salient_findings: Right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1 without significant nerve-root or cord compression
key_facts: 48-year-old woman with a history of asthma
2-day history of right lower-extremity numbness and pain
Denies any low back pain
Manual muscle testing of the right tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus was 3/5
Gastrocnemius and flexor hallucis longus were 4/5
Deep-tendon reflexes were normal
Straight-leg-raising was positive at 70 degrees
Femoral-nerve stretch test was negative
Plain radiographs showed degenerative scoliosis at L5-S1
Lumbar MRI demonstrated a right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1
Initial peroneal-nerve conduction studies revealed a motor conduction velocity of 51.5 m/s
Ankle-brachial indices were decreased
Lower-extremity arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions
Developed right foot drop with muscle strength 1/5
Absent Achilles reflexes bilaterally
Urgent MRI showed no new nerve-root compression
Repeat peroneal conduction studies failed to elicit an evoked myogenic potential

shortlist.label: Lumbar disc herniation
shortlist.why_kept: MRI finding of right-sided disc herniation at L5-S1

shortlist.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower extremity numbness and weakness

shortlist.label: Vasculitic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Decreased ankle-brachial indices and negative arteriography

shortlist.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of muscle weakness and absent Achilles reflexes

raw.rationale: The patient developed right foot drop with significant weakness in muscles innervated by the peroneal nerve, and repeat peroneal conduction studies failed to elicit an evoked myogenic potential, indicating damage to the peroneal nerve.

rejected.label: Lumbar disc herniation
rejected.why: Although the patient had a disc herniation at L5-S1, the urgent MRI showed no new nerve-root compression, and the symptoms cannot be fully explained by the disc herniation alone.

rejected.label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms progressed rapidly, which is not typical for chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy, and there is no clear evidence of demyelination.

rejected.label: Vasculitic neuropathy
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of vasculitis, and the patient's symptoms and test results do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Guillain-Barré syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are localized to one leg, which is not typical for Guillain-Barré syndrome, and there is no clear evidence of widespread nerve damage or demyelination.
